maruko.problem: I needed an automated way to manage my 5000+ bookmarks. Maruko is the third iteration of my ideal automation for managing bookmarks.
maruko.decisions: I wanted it to be hands-off. No collections, no groupings. I wanted it to sort a custom "Recent" folder.
maruko.lessons: The only way to talk to the browser and edit bookmarks is through an extension, so Maruko also ships a browser extension.

mermaido.problem: I write Mermaid diagrams all the time. I wanted a fast, native place to edit the code and see the diagram right away, without a browser tab.
mermaido.decisions: Keep it small: one editor, one preview. Pan, zoom, dark mode, and a way to step through a sequence diagram message by message.
mermaido.lessons: Mermaid loads from a CDN, so Mermaido needs a connection. Bundling it would fix that. A small tool that does one thing is easy to keep using.

clustermap.problem: After playing with treemaps, I thought they could help describe a Kubernetes cluster at a glance (restarts, CPU and memory consumption, and so on).
clustermap.decisions: Clustermap doesn't store credentials. It reuses the configuration stored on the user's machine.
clustermap.lessons: Treemaps are a fast and great way to visualize many things.

gus.problem: I am a big fan of small notation systems. GUS is my first. I needed a way to codify rhythm without taking away expressiveness.
gus.decisions: GUS needed to be small and versatile. I needed to translate many grooves that I know into GUS.
gus.lessons: Small notation systems are a great way to encode information.
